question: Do sparse higher-dimensional expanders exist in every dimension?
idea: Expander graphs connect very effectively without giving each vertex many neighbors. The manuscript claims analogous finite simplicial complexes exist in every dimension, with bounded vertex degrees and uniform coboundary expansion over the two-element field in all lower degrees. These are specific higher-dimensional expansion guarantees, not just visually dense connections.
why: The study of arrangements, networks, and counting. It looks for patterns that must appear when a structure is large or dense enough.

exactClaim: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d ≥ 3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension. )
